oidc_jwt.description: Casdoor issues access_token and id_token with the same JWT payload and treats them as interchangeable in content.
oidc_jwt.note: Do not flag identical claims across access_token and id_token as token confusion by itself; use access_token as the API bearer credential.

oidc_jwt.description: The /api/userinfo response only includes claims allowed by the granted scope and may be minimal.
oidc_jwt.note: Missing profile/email fields in userinfo are expected unless corresponding scopes were requested.

oidc_jwt.description: Casdoor documentation does not describe jti tracking or one-time JWT enforcement for normal OAuth access tokens; replay of the same bearer token is expected until expiry or logout.
oidc_jwt.note: Do not report replay_same_token for ordinary bearer access tokens as a vulnerability unless a stronger one-time guarantee was explicitly configured elsewhere.

oidc_jwt.description: SSO logout invalidates tokens by setting ExpiresIn to 0 or negative and refresh/introspection reject tokens with ExpiresIn <= 0.
oidc_jwt.note: Post-logout token rejection is expected; use it as control behavior, not as evidence of unrelated auth failures.

oidc_jwt.description: When exclusive sign-in is enabled on an application, a new login removes all previous sessions for that user and application.
oidc_jwt.note: Old-session failures after a second login are expected and should not be treated as inconsistent session handling.

oidc_jwt.description: Application tag restrictions do not apply to admins and global admins.
oidc_jwt.note: Authorization tests for tag-based access must use non-admin users to avoid false negatives.

oidc_jwt.description: The /api/userinfo response only includes claims allowed by the scopes requested when the token was issued.
oidc_jwt.note: Missing profile/email/phone/address fields without corresponding scopes is expected.

oidc_jwt.description: Using authorization_code grant with code=guest-user creates a new guest user instead of completing a normal code flow.
oidc_jwt.note: This special code path is a documented extension; do not confuse guest account creation with authorization code substitution.

oidc_jwt.description: Shared applications use an organization-specific suffix in client_id or application name: -org-<organizationName>.
oidc_jwt.note: Org-specific client_id rewriting is by design for shared apps and should not be treated as cross-tenant confusion.

oidc_jwt.description: Casdoor can automatically link OAuth logins to existing users by OAuth identity, email/phone, or username case-insensitively.
oidc_jwt.note: Some apparent cross-user merges are configured linking behavior, not necessarily identity-collision bugs.

oidc_jwt.constraint: Application.expire_in_hours and refresh_expire_in_hours use numeric sentinel semantics: refresh token expiration default is 0 hours, and documentation states 0 means the configured default/disabled-refresh-expiry behavior rather than a literal already-expired token. Never assume 0 means immediate expiry; explicitly set nonzero values when testing token lifetime behavior.

Application.code_resend_timeout uses sentinel semantics: value 0 means use the global default resend timeout, not zero seconds. For deterministic tests involving verification-code timing, set a positive explicit value instead of 0.

For I2 expired_token and future_token tests, include a control token exchange/login using a valid token in the same application configuration. A failed attack token alone is ambiguous because application grant types, redirect URI, client credentials, or scope configuration may also cause failure.

For I3 redirect/resource coherence tests, if the authorization request includes resource, the token request must include the exact same resource value. Casdoor requires exact match between authorize and token requests for RFC 8707 resource indicators; mismatches are by design and must not be reported as flow-binding vulnerabilities.

For I3 PKCE tests, when PKCE is enabled on the application or provider flow, the token request must include code_verifier matching the original code_challenge. With PKCE enabled, client_secret becomes optional but if supplied it must still be correct. Do not interpret failures from missing or wrong code_verifier as unrelated auth bugs.

For I3 config-change sequences on applications, new logins after update_application are expected to use the updated application settings immediately. A valid coherence test must compare behavior of equivalent requests before and after the change, not treat legitimate admin reconfiguration as a vulnerability.

For I5 token_exchange_scope_escalation tests, Casdoor documentation says omitted scope inherits the subject token scope, while provided scope is intended to narrow permissions. Requesting broader scope than the subject token is the correct attack. If the exchanged token simply inherits the original scope when scope is omitted, that is by design.

For I5 audience-binding tests, use the resource parameter on both /login/oauth/authorize and /api/login/oauth/access_token to force the access token aud claim to the target service URI. Without resource, the audience defaults to the client ID, so service-audience tests are invalid.

Redirect URI matching is exact. For all authorization_code tests, the redirect_uri used in start_oidc_auth and exchange_code_for_token must match a configured application Redirect URI character-for-character, including scheme, host, port, path, and trailing slash. Mismatches are setup errors, not security findings.

Casdoor access_token and id_token are documented as identical in payload, but session_token for subsequent API calls must still be mapped to access_token. Do not use id_token as the bearer credential in tests even though the payload is the same.

For multi-tenant tests using shared applications, shared app client identifiers are organization-qualified by appending -org-<organizationName>. Cross-org behavior with shared applications must account for this naming transformation; otherwise apparent audience/client confusion may be a test setup artifact.

Application tags restrict sign-in to users whose user tag set intersects the application's tags, while admins and global admins are exempt. I5 authorization tests using tagged applications must avoid admin users or they will bypass tag restrictions by design.

Exclusive sign-in is a by-design session invalidation feature. If EnableExclusiveSignin is enabled on the application, a second successful login for the same user and application invalidates prior sessions. Multi-session replay or parallel-session tests must disable this setting or account for forced revocation.

For I3 redirect_uri_mismatch and state-bound authorization-code tests, start_oidc_auth and exchange_code_for_token MUST use exactly the same redirect_uri value. Casdoor documentation explicitly requires the resource parameter to match exactly between authorization and token requests, and OAuth callback handling is based on the configured Redirect URL.

For I5 audience/resource-binding tests, use the resource parameter on BOTH /login/oauth/authorize and /api/login/oauth/access_token. Casdoor sets the access token aud claim to the resource URI only when resource is supplied, and the resource must match exactly between the two requests.

For I2 expired_token and future_token style freshness tests against Casdoor-issued tokens, include a CONTROL flow that obtains a valid token from the same application before sending the attack request. Otherwise a failure may be caused by bad client_id/client_secret, redirect_uri mismatch, disabled grant type, or missing PKCE rather than token-time validation.

Refresh token lifetime has sentinel semantics: application Refresh Token expiration default is 0 hours. In Casdoor, 0 does NOT mean immediate expiry; it means the default configured value is used/feature may be effectively disabled until configured. Never assume numeric 0 means literal zero lifetime without checking the application setting.

Code resend timeout has sentinel semantics: application Code resend timeout set to 0 means use the global default, not zero seconds. Do not interpret 0 as 'no wait' in tests that depend on verification-code timing.

CookieExpireInHours has sentinel semantics: application CookieExpireInHours set to 0 means use the default cookie lifetime, not immediate expiration. Do not use 0 when testing session-expiry behavior expecting instant logout.

Casdoor supports PKCE on the authorization code flow. When the application enables PKCE, exchange_code_for_token MUST include code_verifier; client_secret becomes optional but if provided must be correct. Missing code_verifier in a PKCE-enabled app causes flow failure unrelated to the invariant under test.

For I3 config-change sequences involving grant types, the fuzzer MUST ensure the target grant type is enabled on the application before treating a token endpoint failure as a security result. Casdoor enables authorization_code by default, but other grant types such as password and token-exchange must be enabled on the application.

For I5 scope-escalation tests on token_exchange, request a baseline subject token with a limited scope first, then exchange it with a broader requested scope. Casdoor documents that omitted scope inherits the subject token scope, while provided scope is intended for narrowing/subsetting. A broader exchanged scope should be treated as a potential authorization-binding issue.

For I5 audience tests using introspection, authenticate to /api/login/oauth/introspect with HTTP Basic using client_id:client_secret. A 401/403 from introspection without Basic auth is expected and must not be interpreted as token invalidity.

For I4 identity comparisons, Casdoor userinfo returns sub as the stable user identifier UUID, not necessarily the username or email originally supplied during login. Compare granted identity using sub/returned claims with awareness that username may not be echoed by /api/userinfo unless requested via scopes or token parsing.

For I4 multi-organization tests, the same logical application may be referenced with an org-specific suffix when using shared applications: client_id can be transformed as <client_id>-org-<organizationName>. Cross-org behavior must account for this by-design client identifier rewriting rather than treating it as identity confusion.

For I2 replay_same_token against Casdoor-issued bearer JWTs, do NOT flag successful reuse of the same access token as a vulnerability by itself. Casdoor documents stateless JWT/OAuth bearer usage and does not claim one-time-use semantics for access tokens.

For I2 replay_same_token on oidc_jwt, DO NOT flag reuse of the same JWT access token as a vulnerability by itself. Casdoor documents stateless OAuth/OIDC access tokens and does not document jti replay tracking; repeated bearer-token use is by design unless a specific one-time context is being tested.

For I2 expired_token and future_token tests, always run a CONTROL flow first using a valid token request and successful /api/userinfo call. Without a control, a failed attack flow may be caused by bad client_id/client_secret, redirect_uri mismatch, missing grant enablement, or other setup errors rather than time-claim enforcement.

For I3 redirect_uri_mismatch tests, the redirect_uri used at /login/oauth/authorize and /api/login/oauth/access_token must match exactly. Casdoor documentation states redirect URIs are configured exactly and callback/redirect mismatches break the flow; do not interpret such failures as session-binding bugs.

For I3 PKCE tests, when PKCE is enabled you must send code_challenge and code_challenge_method=S256 at /login/oauth/authorize and the original code_verifier at /api/login/oauth/access_token. If client_secret is also sent, it must be correct. Missing or wrong code_verifier causes expected flow failure, not an identity-binding issue.

For I5 audience/resource binding tests, if you use the resource parameter at authorization time you MUST send the same exact resource value again in the token request. Casdoor states the resource must match exactly between authorization and token requests, and the resulting access token aud becomes the resource URI instead of the client ID.

For I5 token_exchange_scope_escalation tests, Casdoor documents that requested scope during token exchange should be a subset of the original token scope, and omitting scope inherits the original scope. The fuzzer must compare exchanged-token scope/claims against the original authorization and treat inherited-scope behavior as expected.

For I5 token_exchange subject token type tests, only the documented subject_token_type values are valid: urn:ietf:params:oauth:token-type:access_token, urn:ietf:params:oauth:token-type:jwt, and urn:ietf:params:oauth:token-type:id_token. Rejections for other token types are expected setup failures.

Numeric sentinel: application Refresh Token expiration default is 0 hours. In Casdoor, value 0 does not mean immediate expiry; it is the documented default setting for refresh-token expiration and must not be assumed to disable refresh or force instant expiration. Tests that rely on refresh-token lifetime must explicitly configure a nonzero value and not infer semantics from 0.

Numeric sentinel: application Code resend timeout uses 0 as 'use the global default', not literal zero seconds. Do not assume 0 disables throttling or allows immediate resend; explicit nonzero values are required for deterministic resend-timing tests.

Numeric sentinel: token invalidation on SSO logout is represented by ExpiresIn <= 0. Zero or negative ExpiresIn means invalidated token, not a usable zero-lifetime token. Freshness tests that inspect token state after logout must treat ExpiresIn <= 0 as revoked/expired by design.

For I4 multi-organization tests, Casdoor user identity is organization-scoped. Usernames are identified as <organization>/<username>, and shared applications append -org-<organizationName> to client_id/application references. Do not compare identities across organizations using bare username alone.

For I4 case-confusion and account-linking tests involving upstream OAuth identities, Casdoor may automatically link OAuth logins to existing users by OAuth identity, email/phone if enabled, or username case-insensitively. This can intentionally merge identities that look distinct to the fuzzer; verify whether linking settings explain the result before flagging a collision.

For I4 username derivation tests against upstream providers, some providers intentionally map non-sub claims to Casdoor usernames: Lark prefers UserId then UnionId then OpenId; DingTalk uses unionid; Baidu may use a masked username. Do not assume upstream OIDC sub or display name becomes the Casdoor username for federated-provider logins.

For I5 scope/authorization tests against /api/userinfo, returned fields depend on the scope requested when obtaining the access token. Missing profile/email/address/phone fields without corresponding scopes is expected and must not be treated as authorization loss or identity corruption.

For I5 address-claim tests, token format matters. Only JWT-Standard produces an OIDC-compliant address object; JWT, JWT-Empty, and JWT-Custom return address as a raw string array. Do not flag non-object address claims as bugs unless the application is explicitly configured for JWT-Standard.

For I5 custom-scope tests, custom scopes are available only for applications with category Agent. Default applications expose only standard OAuth/OIDC scopes. Do not request custom scopes from non-Agent apps and interpret rejection as a vulnerability.

For I3 config-change sequences involving exclusive sign-in, a new successful login may intentionally terminate prior sessions for the same user and application. Subsequent failures of the old session are by design and must not be interpreted as incoherent session handling.
